long-covid.title: SARS-CoV-2 seeds IAPP aggregation and β-cell failure.
long-covid.authors: Song, Zhiqi, Xu, Yanfeng, Zhao, Wenjie, Zhang, Ling et al.
long-covid.excerpt: The global diabetes incidence has surged post-COVID-19, yet how SARS-CoV-2 drives long-term beta cell (β-cell) failure remains incompletely elucidated. We identified a mechanism whereby SARS-CoV-2 structural proteins directly hijack islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP) to induce pathogenic amyloid deposition, disrupting insulin granule maturation, trafficking, and secretion in an age-susceptible islet microenvironment.

gulf-war-illness.title: Deposition, Retention, and Clearance of Depleted Uranium and Tungsten Following Inhalation Exposure: Biokinetic Analysis and Implications for Long-term Health Effects.
gulf-war-illness.authors: Keifer, Lydia J, Mate-Kole, Emmanuel Matey, Dewji, Shaheen Azim
gulf-war-illness.excerpt: This study evaluates respiratory deposition and subsequent biokinetic behavior of DU and W aerosols using computational modeling informed by reported military exposure conditions. Particle deposition fractions in the respiratory tract were calculated using REDCALdep, which implements the ICRP Publication 66 respiratory tract deposition model with relevant updates from ICRP Publication 130.

pots.title: The link between inflammation and autonomic dysfunction in alpha-synucleinopathies - narrative review.
pots.authors: Kutyłowski, Karol, Alster, Piotr, Madetko-Alster, Natalia
pots.excerpt: Alpha-synucleinopathies are a group of disorders characterized by the accumulation of the pathological form of alpha-synuclein. This group comprises Parkinson's disease, Parkinson's disease dementia, multiple system atrophy, dementia with Lewy bodies, pure autonomic failure, and idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder.

pots.title: Targeting Brain-Body Processes in Postural Tachycardia Syndrome: A Pilot Trial of POts Reprocessing Therapy.
pots.authors: Crouch, Taylor B, Chase, Spencer, Redman, Tammy, Wells, Mary et al.
pots.excerpt: Purpose Postural tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is a chronic autonomic disorder characterized by orthostatic intolerance and frequently accompanied by a broad constellation of debilitating symptoms. Emerging evidence suggests that dysregulation within central-autonomic regulatory networks may contribute to symptom persistence.

mcas.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
mcas.authors: Luo, Zhengrong, Zhang, Youwen, Ge, Xiaolei, Tian, Xinyi et al.
mcas.excerpt: Based on the distribution characteristics of mast cells and existing mechanistic evidence, the study explores the potential biological effects of shallow needling control (sham-acupuncture). Regarding cellular distribution, mast cells exhibit a physiological characteristic of dense distribution in both the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, predominantly in the distal regions, and show a higher density in acupoint...

mcas.title: Type I autoimmunity in chronic spontaneous urticaria: Evidence, limits, and endotype overlap.
mcas.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
mcas.authors: Konstantinou, George N, Grattan, Clive E H
mcas.excerpt: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) is a mast cell-driven disorder with basophil involvement and several possible upstream mechanisms. Type IIb autoimmune CSU, mediated by functional IgG autoantibodies against FcεRIα or IgE, is the best-validated endotype.

mcas.title: Systemic Allergic Reactions to mRNA COVID-19 Vaccines: A Randomized Placebo-controlled Trial.
mcas.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
mcas.authors: Wheatley, Lisa M, Baker, James R, Adkinson, N Franklin, Gruchalla, Rebecca et al.
mcas.excerpt: COVID-19 mRNA vaccines were associated in early reports with more allergic reactions than most vaccines, especially in people with allergic histories. To estimate the proportions of systemic allergic reactions to mRNA COVID-19 vaccines in people reporting prior severe allergic reactions to various allergens, and/or mast cell disorders (PSAR/MCD Group) and determine if proportions are higher than in non-PSAR/non-MCD...

mcas.title: Estradiol-associated extracellular signaling in the human breast
mcas.authors: Abrahamsson, Annelie, Wang, Xingyue, Zhong, Wen, Dabrosin, Charlotta
mcas.excerpt: Sex steroid exposure is a major risk factor for breast cancer initiation and progression through incompletely understood mechanisms. Novel therapeutics for prevention and treatment of estrogen-dependent breast cancer are needed.

mcas.title: Luteolin alleviates neurogenic inflammation in OVA-induced combined allergic rhinitis and asthma syndrome mice through TRPV1/ERK-related signaling.
mcas.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
mcas.authors: Li, Jing, Mirodilova, Firuza, Lei, Lei
mcas.excerpt: Combined Allergic Rhinitis and Asthma Syndrome (CARAS), a common chronic allergic respiratory disease, involves dysregulated neuro-immune interactions and neurogenic inflammation. Luteolin (LUT) has significant anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities.

mcas.title: LL-37-MRGPRX2-Mast Cell Signaling in Rosacea: Current Evidence and Directions for Human Studies.
mcas.excerpt: This critical narrative review examines evidence relevant to LL-37-Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 (MRGPRX2)-mast-cell signaling in rosacea and considers the relevance of these findings to future human studies. Literature was identified through PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection searches, supplemented by examination of reference lists from relevant original studies and recent reviews.

mcas.title: Inducible Laryngeal Obstruction in Hypermobile Patients.
mcas.authors: Menton, Stacey M, Fairweather, DeLisa, Wilson, Frances C, Zangerle, Derek J et al.
mcas.excerpt: To determine whether patients with hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (hEDS) or hypermobility spectrum disorders (HSD) and inducible laryngeal obstruction (ILO) have more voice, cough, swallowing, GI issues, and MC activation than patients without ILO. This retrospective study of 2162 patients meeting 2017 diagnostic criteria for hEDS (n = 507) or HSD (n = 1655) who were seen at the EDS Clinic in Mayo Clinic Florida...

mcas.title: Mast cell activation syndrome: Global perspectives from a World Allergy Organization survey on knowledge, diagnosis, and access to care.
mcas.authors: Giavina-Bianchi, Pedro, Giavina-Bianchi, Mara, Morais-Almeida, Mário, Álvarez-Twose, Iván et al.
mcas.excerpt: Mast Cell Activation Syndrome (MCAS) has emerged as a highly debated and increasingly recognized condition in allergy and clinical immunology. Despite established AIM/ECNM consensus criteria, major uncertainties persist regarding its diagnosis, implementation in real-world practice, and equitable access to diagnostic resources worldwide.

mcas.title: Food-Associated Kounis Syndrome: Clinical Spectrum and Diagnostic Considerations from a Case Report and Systematic Qualitative Synthesis of Published Cases.
mcas.authors: Sanchez-Fernandez, Sergio, Lasarte, Gabriel Gastaminza, Garófalo, Carmen D'Amelio, Paredes-Gutierrez et al.
mcas.excerpt: Kounis syndrome (KS) is a hypersensitivity-associated acute coronary syndrome. Food-associated KS remains poorly characterized, and its clinical presentation may be mimicked by non-immune food-related toxic reactions.

mcas.title: The dual and context-dependent role of mast cells in cutaneous wound healing and scar formation.
mcas.excerpt: Successful tissue repair depends on the precise orchestration of phase-specific cellular responses alongside sustained activity of multifunctional immune regulators. Mast cells, which have primarily been long regarded as effector cells of allergic reactions, have emerged as pivotal modulators of wound repair.

mcas.title: Mechanistic insight into eosinophilic enteritis and related disorders.
mcas.authors: Syverson, Erin P, Venkatesh, Rajitha D, Bailey, Dominique D
mcas.excerpt: Eosinophilic gastrointestinal diseases (EGIDs) affecting the gastrointestinal tract outside of the esophagus are categorized as non-EoE EGIDs, and knowledge regarding their natural history and pathophysiology is rapidly advancing. This review synthesizes evolving mechanistic insights in non-EoE EGID immunopathogenesis, emerging paradigms of disease development, and how these insights influence potential therapeutic...

mcas.title: Imperatorin exerts anti-colorectal cancer effects by targeting NOX2 to inhibit mast cell degranulation.
mcas.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
mcas.authors: Shi, Xianpeng, Zhang, Peng, Cui, Xia, Hou, Yajing et al.
mcas.excerpt: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major global malignancy with a poor prognosis in advanced stages. Aberrant mast cell activation within the tumor microenvironment (TME) drives CRC progression; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying the tumor-promoting role of mast cells in the hypoxic TME remain unclear, and effective therapies targeting these cells are lacking.

other-post-viral.title: Metabolic basis of post-infectious sequelae after Ebola virus disease.
other-post-viral.journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society
other-post-viral.authors: Sanford, Anna C, Bond, Nell G, Ficenec, Samuel, Osterman, Charlotte et al.
other-post-viral.excerpt: Ebola virus disease (EVD) survivors often present with clinical sequelae after acute disease resolution, called post-Ebola syndrome (PES). Why some survivors develop these sequelae and others do not is poorly defined.
